• Constraint — "Relational expansion in get_relevant_context must be bounded: budgeted reach, not neighborhood dump"
  hasDescription: Commit 5dc4a3ba00 (src/graph/mod.rs, EXPAND_FROM_TOP/EXPAND_MAX_HOPS/EXPAND_MAX constants). Relational expansion in get_relevant_context is a budgeted reach to the few linked records that complete an answer — specifically the lexically-distant neighbor that BM25 alone misses — without dumping the full neighborhood. Concretely: expansion seeds from only the top-N BM25 hits (EXPAND_FROM_TOP=3), walks at most EXPAND_MAX_HOPS=2 hops outward, and appends at most EXPAND_MAX=5 total linked records. Context efficiency is the whole point of get_relevant_context: returning the entire reachable neighborhood would negate the retrieval tool's purpose of surfacing the most relevant records without overwhelming the caller's context window. Expansion is skipped entirely for list-all calls and when MOOSEDEV_EXPAND_HOPS=0.
  hasAuthor: James Adam <jcadam@startmail.com>

  hasTitle: Relational expansion in get_relevant_context must be bounded: budgeted reach, not neighborhood dump

• ArchitecturalDecision — "Benchmark oracle mode: harness-side retrieval isolates knowledge-value from fetch-willingness"
  hasDescription: Commit 29cac60c28 (`bench/run.py`). A `mode="oracle"` parameter on `run_cell()` causes the harness to retrieve relevant knowledge and prepend it verbatim to the prompt, without giving the agent a live memory tool. This isolates two confounds: H8 (fetch-willingness — whether the agent chooses to call the memory tool) and knowledge-value (whether the knowledge itself helps). If oracle does not beat B0, the captured knowledge has no value; if live-tool < oracle, the gap is fetch-willingness alone.

Implementation: `oracle_context()` calls `get_relevant_context` for B2 (current-only, symbolic BM25); `freetext_oracle_context()` runs BM25 over the exported chunk file for B1 arms (currency-blind — superseded chunks are retrievable, same as what a B1-rag agent would get). Topic is `task["memory_topic"] or task["prompt"]` — a focused subject phrase so the retrieval signal is unambiguous.

Oracle asymmetry is intentional: the B2−B1 oracle delta isolates B2's currency-awareness (the agent acting on lifecycle status) rather than information withholding (B1 oracle would also retrieve superseded chunks, so if B2 oracle correctly ignores a superseded record and B1 oracle uses it, that gap is earned).
  hasAuthor: James Adam <jcadam@startmail.com>
  hasLifecycleStatus: accepted
  hasTitle: Benchmark oracle mode: harness-side retrieval isolates knowledge-value from fetch-willingness
  hasTimestamp: 2026-06-19T19:27:46Z

• Lesson — "Don't index instance data for A-box recall — MOOSE walk planning beats vector search for precision and auditability"
  hasDescription: Commit 17bcfda8 / tasks/lessons.md addition. Pattern surfaced during investigation of `get_relevant_context` imprecision: the temptation was to improve recall quality via embedding-ranked A-box recall or embedding-based instance dedup — building a vector index over recorded instance content. This contradicts a deliberate MOOSE design choice: MOOSE deliberately does NOT index instance data; walk planning was devised to avoid the vector-index/RAG trap and deliver more precise, auditable retrieval.

Rule: when recall, dedup, or contradiction detection seems to need "semantic search" over recorded instances, reach for the symbolic path first — `query` (walk planning) and `sparql` for retrieval precision; LLM-as-sensor + typed conflict for contradiction — not a nearest-neighbor index over instances. Embeddings in MOOSEDev are confined to T-box term alignment (`suggest_parent`) over the static ontology (class placement, not instance retrieval). `get_relevant_context` is a shallow lexical anchor/browse tool by construction; fix its imprecision with an honesty floor + tool-selection guidance, not vector search.
  hasAuthor: James Adam <jcadam@startmail.com>
  hasLifecycleStatus: accepted
  learnedFrom: https://moosedev.dev/kg/ArchitecturalDecision/03d8d242-c154-4b55-8b3b-781289fbcb6c

• ArchitecturalDecision — "get_relevant_context topic search: search_records (BM25 over label + description) replaces search_classes (label-only)"
  hasDescription: Commit caa6e387e6 (Merge search-records-integration). src/graph/mod.rs relevant_context(): entity_index.search_classes(t, &class_iris, &state.store, &data_graphs, moose::LABEL_PREDICATES, limit) replaced by entity_index.search_records(t, &class_iris, &state.store, &data_graphs, &text_fields, limit). text_fields = [(moose::RDFS_LABEL, 2.0_f32), (state.capture.description.as_str(), 1.0_f32)] — rdfs:label weighted 2× because every record carries it as its title; description weighted 1×. Searching rdfs:label rather than hasTitle ensures label-only records (no hasTitle) are still found and the title text isn't double-counted. BM25 is raw/corpus-relative — results are ranked and top-k selected rather than filtered by an absolute score. List-all path (no topic → list_instances via SPARQL) is unchanged. Tool remains purely symbolic: no LLM on the retrieval path.

Commit caa6e387e6 switches to entity_index.search_records() with BM25 weighted text fields (rdfs:label × 2.0, hasDescription × 1.0), covering both the primary label and the richer description content. The symbolic (no-LLM) constraint is preserved; only the matching surface expands.

• Requirement — "Bootstrap must produce typed edges so relational expansion reaches lexically-distant context"
  hasDescription: skills/bootstrap-existing-codebase.md (commit 9114ee7a73, intro rewrite): "only a linked graph lets you follow 'why?' from a decision to rationale that lives in a lexically-distant record. Flat keyword retrieval finds a single record; only a linked graph lets you follow." The bootstrap workflow exists partly to seed the graph for get_relevant_context relational expansion — but expansion only reaches linked neighbors; if bootstrap produces only isolated nodes, the expansion step is useless. Therefore the bootstrap must write typed edges, not just typed nodes.

• ArchitecturalDecision — "get_relevant_context: bounded relational expansion follows record→record edges from BM25 seeds"
  hasDescription: Commit 5dc4a3ba00 (src/graph/mod.rs relevant_context() + record_neighbors()). After BM25 retrieval produces a ranked seed set, get_relevant_context performs a bounded hop-walk over outbound record→record edges (record_neighbors()) to surface lexically-distant records that are linked to the seeds but would be missed by pure keyword matching. Implementation details:

- record_neighbors(iri): enumerates all outbound quads from a project-graph subject in the project KG graph. Skips rdf:type, prov: metadata firehose, and hasRationale (its text is already inlined by build_context_item). Returns (predicate_local, neighbor_iri, neighbor_class) for neighbors that pass require_information_record — only recorded knowledge items, not arbitrary graph nodes.

- Expansion loop: seeds from the top EXPAND_FROM_TOP=3 BM25 hits; walks up to EXPAND_MAX_HOPS=2 hops; appends at most EXPAND_MAX=5 total neighbor items to the result (hard cap). Each appended item gets a "linkedVia" synthetic property showing which predicate led to it.

- Guards: skipped entirely for list-all calls (topic=None or whitespace-only) and when MOOSEDEV_EXPAND_HOPS=0 (or env var override to any other value). include_history filter applies to expanded items too.

Rationale: BM25 ranks by shared tokens — a Constraint whose title shares no tokens with the query but is linked via isMotivatedBy from a matching ArchitecturalDecision is invisible to BM25 alone. Traversal reaches it in one hop. The bounded budget (Constraint f28b0186) ensures this does not become a neighborhood dump that defeats context efficiency. The symbolic-layer principle is preserved: no LLM involvement on the expansion path.

• Pattern — "Agent recall-first protocol for self-hosted MCP: get_relevant_context → short NLQ → record → align_concepts → validate"
  hasDescription: Commit 85cd7821cc (CLAUDE.md "Dogfooding MOOSEDev" section). Codifies the operating discipline for agents using the self-hosted MCP: (1) Recall first — get_relevant_context or query before non-trivial work; (2) Keep NLQ questions short — one focused sentence per query call; (3) Capture as you go — record_important_decision with kind ArchitecturalDecision/Lesson/Constraint/Pattern/AntiPattern/Requirement; capture decision + rationale, not transient chatter; (4) Align new concepts with align_concepts before introducing a new term to prevent model graph drift (Invariant #4); (5) Verify with validate_against_architecture after capturing; use sparql for precise deterministic reads. Rationale: makes agent use of MOOSEDev reliable and disciplined — recall prevents duplication, alignment prevents drift, validation ensures consistency. Explicitly stated: "When its tools are available, prefer them over re-deriving context (invariant #5)."

• ArchitecturalDecision — "Benchmark four-arm design: B0 (none) / B1-md (markdown) / B1-rag (BM25) / B2 (MOOSEDev graph)"
  hasDescription: Commit 7633402925 ("initial benchmark work") introduces the `bench/` harness with four evaluation arms, each receiving the same questions but with different agent-memory configurations:

- **B0** (baseline): no memory tool — the agent answers from raw project files only. AGENTS.md instructs "answer as accurately as you can from the information available to you."
- **B1-md**: project knowledge exported as markdown files under `docs/decisions/`; agent is told to grep/read those files before answering. Tests text-based recall from a flat file system.
- **B1-rag**: same knowledge as B2, exported as text chunks and served via a BM25 `recall` MCP tool (`bench/freetext_mcp/server.py`). Tests lexical free-text retrieval over the same record set.
- **B2**: MOOSEDev graph arm — agent uses `get_relevant_context`, `sparql`, and `query` tools against the real graph.

Rationale: the B0 baseline measures the model's raw knowledge; B1-md measures structured-docs-without-recall-tools; B1-rag and B2 carry **identical knowledge content** (content parity, see companion Constraint) so the B2−B1-rag gap isolates the symbolic retrieval layer's contribution over equivalent free-text RAG. BM25 is the initial B1 retriever (skeleton); upgrade to embedding retriever is noted in the code for the full matrix.

item.text: `get_relevant_context` currently does a symbolic BM25 lookup over recorded items, searching `rdfs:label` and `description` with label weighted higher, then returns the top-ranked matches. It can also do a bounded graph walk from the top 3 seed hits, following record-to-record edges for up to 2 hops and at most 5 extra linked records, to catch lexically distant but connected context.
